newsitem.title: UK: UK general election not later than May 1 - Major.
newsitem.headline: UK general election not later than May 1 - Major.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday he would hold a general election on or before May 1.
"It's certainly not going to be later (than May 1). You can be absolutely certain about that," Major told BBC radio.
"But I am not going to give you a date this morning," he added.
The latest possible date Major could wait before holding a general election is May 22, 1997.
The opposition Labour Party, well ahead in opinion polls, has repeatedly urged Major to hold a general election as soon as possible.
Major is widely expected to wait until the last moment in the hope that an improving economy will boost the electoral chances of his Conservative Party.

Most recent opinion polls have put the Conservatives around 20 points behind Labour, although the latest said the gap had narrowed to 14 points. The Conservatives have been in power in Britain for an unbroken 17 years.
The government on Wednesday set out its legislative programme for the last session of parliament before an election.
The bills, listed in a speech given by Queen Elizabeth, included measures to put criminals in jail for longer and tighten school discipline.
